name: Theresa Ericksen
story: Served as an Army nurse at Sternberg Army Hospital in Chickamauga, Georgia, during the Spanish-American War, in Manila during the Philippine-American War, and in France during World War I. She later worked to establish Fort Snelling as a national cemetery, where she now rests.

name: George DeJean DeBeeson
story: A Nebraska farm boy with an eighth-grade education and a gift for invention, he helped build an airplane of piano wire, canvas, and bicycle tires in 1914. He enlisted in the Navy Reserve in October 1918 and trained briefly as an aviator. By 1931 he had built the "Iron Skull," an early autopilot.

name: Deloris Louise Ruddock
story: One of 855 African American women in the 6888th Central Postal Directory Battalion, the "Six Triple Eight." Their unit was given six months to clear a two-year backlog of mail in England and finished in three, then cleared another backlog in France. After the war she used her GI Bill to study fashion in New York.

name: Julia Nashanany Reeves
story: A member of the Potawatomi Tribe from Crandon, Wisconsin, she joined the Army Nurse Corps in 1942. With the 53rd Evacuation Hospital in New Caledonia, she helped treat 6,000 patients in six months, then served in England and again in the Korean War. Her tribe honored her with an eagle feather as an honored warrior.

name: Jose Antonio Muniz-Vazquez
branch: U.S. Army Air Forces / Air Force
story: Born in Ponce, Puerto Rico, he flew 20 combat missions over China, Burma, and India in World War II and was recalled for Korea. He later commanded the Puerto Rico Air National Guard's 198th Fighter Squadron. He died when his F-86D lost power during takeoff for a July 4, 1960, flyover. Muniz Air National Guard Base is named for him.

name: Robert J. Raymond
branch: U.S. Navy (WWII), then U.S. Marine Corps
story: Served on a Navy destroyer in the Pacific in World War II, then enlisted in the Marines when the Korean War began. He landed at Inchon and fought at the Chosin Reservoir with the 1st Marine Division. He was killed on July 26, 1953, in the war's final hours, and was awarded the Navy Cross and Purple Heart.

name: Robert Wayne "Bob" Monroe
story: A Vietnam combat Marine who rose to gunnery sergeant. His VLM page is one of the fullest on the site, with a biography, service timeline, photos, documents, and many tributes. His widow, Linda, posts to it about once a month, on anniversaries and days that matter to her.

name: Eric Ulysses Ramirez
branch: U.S. Navy, then California Army National Guard
story: The son of farm workers who emigrated from Mexico, he served in the Navy and then joined the California National Guard while working as a San Diego County sheriff's deputy. Deployed to Iraq with the 670th Military Police Company, he was killed in an ambush on February 12, 2004, six weeks before he was due home. "He always had that smile," a fellow soldier said.

name: Karl Richard Linn
story: He co-founded his Midlothian, Virginia, high school's FIRST robotics team and joined the Marine Corps Reserve after 9/11 while studying engineering at VCU. A combat engineer, he was mortally wounded near Haditha Dam, Iraq, on January 26, 2005. A VCU robotics scholarship carries his name.

name: Jeremiah Thomas Wittman
story: Born in Billings, Montana, he loved dirt bike racing, hunting, and grilling outside. After two tours in Iraq, he deployed to Afghanistan as a mortarman and was killed by an IED in February 2010. He received the Bronze Star and Purple Heart.
